text:
alex: Heads-up — ACME (acct: acme-prod-42) flagged a marketplace invoice mismatch. AWS invoice line items show $1,230.00 labeled 'Redwood Inference usage' for Feb, but our billing dashboard shows $982.40 after credits. Customer thinks they were double-charged for marketplace credits. Can someone triage?

morgan: ACK. Can you paste the invoice line (screenshot or text) and the dashboard export? Also need marketplace entitlement ID if available.

ajex: Posting cropped invoice lines from customer (redacted):
```
Invoice 2026-02-28
LineItem: 2026-02  Redwd-Prod-Usage    $1,230.00
Discount: AWS Credit Applied            -$200.00
Tax                                      $10.00
Total                                    $1,040.00
```
They say our console shows $982.40 after our credits of $257.60 applied.

jess: I exported ACME's usage CSV from the console for Feb and the /v1/usage report for their marketplace account. Key rows: 
```
2026-02-01, generation, tokens=1,200,000, cost_usd=620.00
2026-02-12, embeddings, tokens=300,000, cost_usd=120.00
2026-02-21, generation, tokens=400,000, cost_usd=242.40
Subtotal usage: 982.40
Credits applied (promo+partner): 257.60
Net: 724.80
```
That net (724.80) is not what customer sees either. Something off between marketplace gross vs our net.

raj: Two common mismatch causes: (1) marketplace shows gross pre-partner-credit, or includes a provider surcharge line, (2) our usage vs marketplace metering service using different metering IDs/timezones. Do we have the Marketplace Metering Service ID from ACME?

morgan: Customer sent this: Marketplace Metering Service ID: 567890123456. Also attached AWS invoice line CSV (they filtered to our product).

billing-bot: Automated note — invoice 2026-02 for account acme-prod-42 received via connector. Invoice UUID: inv-2026-02-acme-9a. Parsed line items: provider_charge=$1,230.00, provider_credit_applied=$200.00. Reconciled_charge_to_internal=$1,030.00 (pre-tax).

emily: I ran a quick diff of provider_charge vs our dashboard: provider_charge ($1,230) - our dashboard subtotal ($982.40) = $247.60 delta. That's suspiciously close to their reported credits ($257.60) but not exact. Could be rounding or timezone bucket differences.

alex: Customer claims they already received a marketplace promotional credit from AWS for $200 and an additional partner credit $57.60 applied as a manual adjustment in our console. If AWS applied the credit on their invoice but our connector didn't pull the partner adjustment, amounts won't match.

raj: Checklist for triage I recommend:
1) Pull raw marketplace invoice CSV and compare each line item id to our internal metering records (metering_record_id).
2) Check ingestion time for invoice (billing-bot logs) vs when credits were applied in our console.
3) Confirm whether AWS includes partner/manual adjustments as separate line items or merges them into final total.
4) Recompute net charges using the marketplace line items and our credit table.

jess: Quick repro commands I ran for ACME (redacted):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage?account=acme-prod-42&start=2026-02-01&end=2026-02-28&group_by=line_item"
# returns CSV with fields: date,category,tokens,cost_usd,credit_applied,net_cost
```
Output snippet: `2026-02-12,embeddings,300000,120.00,0.00,120.00` (no credit shown for that row).

morgan: Good catch. If our usage row doesn't show credit_applied, then the partner credit might be recorded as a separate ledger entry not tied to usage rows. Emily, can you query ledger entries for acct acme-prod-42 for Feb?

emily: Done. Found two ledger entries: 
- ledger-98765: partner_credit, amount=-57.60, applied_on=2026-03-02, source="manual-adjustment"
- ledger-98766: aws_marketplace_credit, amount=-200.00, applied_on=2026-02-28, source="marketplace-sync"
Note: partner_credit was applied AFTER Feb period (Mar 2). That explains why AWS invoice shows both credits but our Feb dashboard export (snapshot taken 2026-02-28 23:59) didn't include the manual -57.60.

alex: So timeline mismatch. AWS invoice included the partner credit in their final PDF, but our dashboard snapshot we exported before manual adjustment. Customer saw invoice (they looked at PDF dated Mar 3) and thought we double-charged.

raj: Action items:
- Emily to annotate ledger with marketplace invoice UUID and mark partner_credit link to invoice (owner: emily) — ETA 2h.
- Morgan to open AWS Marketplace case referencing inv-2026-02-acme-9a asking for invoice line timestamp + if provider-level credits were applied at invoice generation vs post-processing — ETA EOD.
- Jess to provide the customer a clear timeline + interim credit explanation and offer to issue a one-time adjustment if needed while we wait on AWS case (owner: jess) — ETA 4h.

morgan: AWS case created: case 220334-aws with subject "Clarify credits applied to invoice inv-2026-02-acme-9a". I included meter service ID and our parsed invoice. Assigned to AWS Billing Support.

billing-bot: Note added to thread: reconciliation_status=investigating, presumed_cause=timeline-credit-lag.

alex: Customer update draft (jess please review): "Thanks — we looked into this and see AWS included a marketplace credit on the invoice, and we applied an additional partner credit after our initial dashboard snapshot. This timing difference led to the discrepancy. We are working with AWS to confirm invoice timestamps and will post a final reconciliation. If you'd like, we can issue a temporary account credit while we confirm."

emily: I linked ledger-98765 to inv-2026-02-acme-9a and updated our internal notes. Once AWS confirms, we can either let the invoice stand or issue a charge adjustment/refund.

jess: Customer replied: "OK thanks, please keep us posted. We don't want duplicate charges; if you issue a temporary credit that would be appreciated." :thumbsup:

alex: Closing notes: root cause likely timing/ingestion of manual partner adjustment. Marking thread owner: emily for ledger link and morgan for AWS case. Will update when AWS responds.
